title: Leading his own band at the Savoy in 1946, then Willie Bryant
summary: Mr. Buchanan promised a house-band slot, but Tab Smith's group got it and he lost money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Uh huh, that's quite interesting. And what band did you go to from there -- you stayed six years with Lucky's band.
Yeah, I stayed six years with Lucky's band, and then I organized my own band.

I went in to the Savoy -- Mr. Buchanan had promised me to bring a band into the Savoy, and if the dancers liked the band, he would use me as the house band because the Savoy Sultans had broken up, and they were looking for a small band to take their place.
It was a small band, then, huh?
That was 1946. And it didn't last too long -- I think we stayed up there for two months, and
there was a choice between Tab Smith and myself, and with Tab having a bigger name to start out with ...
Yeah, he was a saxophone soloist.

Yeah, a saxophone soloist, and he had a pretty well-founded reputation, why, he got the job for being in the house band there. In fact, I lost a little bit of money in that band, because I used my own money that I had saved up to buy music and a music stand and the whole bit, you know?

And so after that, Willie Bryant reorganized a band, because he had been out of the band business, he was like a master of ceremonies, and he reorganized a band and in this band we had Bill Dogett who was on piano, and --
You went in Willie Bryant's band?
